messages:
oliver: Heads-up — we got a spike of user sessions that were supposed to stay on stable but started routing to canary after a region failover. Repro rate ~4% of sessions.
maya: hmm, any common header or cookie pattern? can you paste the routing config used for that rollout?
oliver: pasting the rollout policy that was active:
```
{"traffic_split": [{"variant": "stable","weight": 9800},{"variant": "canary","weight": 200}], "sticky": {"mode": "cookie", "name": "sid", "ttl": 86400}, "guards": [{"type": "region_preference","preferred": "us-west-2"}]}
```
james: looks straightforward. Did the failover change the cookie domain/path? That can invalidate sticky and fallback to hash split which might bias small buckets.
priya: user reports include cookie present and same sid value, attached logs show the router attempted to set cookie again after 502 from stable pool.
kevin: logs from edge:
```
router: route_lookup user=uid:12345 sid=abcd1234 -> pool=stable (healthy), attempt=1
router: pool=stable response=502, fallback_policy=REASSIGN
router: recompute_bucket by hash(user) -> bucket=canary
```
maya: ah — REASSIGN fallback is our preemptive policy that re-evaluates split by hashed user key. That can break stickiness if the cookie hasn't been refreshed before subsequent requests.
oliver: but the cookie was present, why did router ignore it? there’s a conditional path where cookie parsing is skipped if the pool had transient error — I think that's the line.
james: that path was added to reduce tail latency for backends that repeatedly 502 during health flaps. It forces a deterministic hash routing to avoid repeated retries to failing backends.
kevin: problem is deterministic hash chooses canary more often for low-weight variants due to modulus skew when user ids are short. We saw a similar skew with the modulo seed when rolling small canaries.
sara: from product POV customers expect stickiness across intermittent failures. We can't silently move them to canary.
priya: suggested quick mitigation: change fallback_policy from REASSIGN to RETRY-COOKIED — try refresh cookie and honor it before recomputing. Low-risk config change.
maya: agree. Also need a long-term fix: make recompute_bucket consider both cookie and header tiebreaker before stepping to hash. And add telemetry metric for "sticky-ignored-due-to-fallback".
james: will open a PR to tweak router flow + add unit tests for failover paths. I'll also add a small sim script to measure bucket skew with small canary weights.
oliver: OK. Action items: @james PR for router change, @priya apply temporary policy override for the affected rollout, @kevin add alert for >1% sessions shifted during failover. @sara I'll add a note to release docs for expected behavior until fix.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: router-service patch-2026-04-06 (canary) -> deployment window 10:30 UTC
oliver: thanks everyone. capturing notes and I'll follow up with postmortem if needed.
